text: Two coherent light sources having intensity in the ratio 2x produce an interference pattern. The ratio $\frac{I_{\max }-I_{\min }}{I_{\max }+I_{\min }}$ will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\frac{I_{1}}{I_{2}}=2x$

We know,

$\frac{I_{\max }}{I_{\min }}=\left (\frac{\sqrt{I_{1}}+\sqrt{I_{2}}}{\sqrt{I_{1}}-\sqrt{I_{2}}}\right )^{2}$

$=\left (\frac{\sqrt{\frac{I1}{I2}}+1}{\sqrt{\frac{I1}{I2}}-1}\right )^{2}$

$=\left (\frac{\sqrt{2x}+1}{\sqrt{2x}-1}\right )^{2}$

Now, 

$\frac{I_{\max }-I_{\min }}{I_{\max }+I_{\min }}$

$=\frac{\frac{I\max }{I\min }-1}{\frac{I\max }{I\min }+1}$

$=\frac{\left (\frac{\sqrt{2x}+1}{\sqrt{2x}-1}\right )^{2}-1}{\left (\frac{\sqrt{2x}+1}{\sqrt{2x}-1}\right )^{2}+1}$

$=\frac{\left (\sqrt{2x}+1\right )^{2}-\left (\sqrt{2x}-1\right )^{2}}{\left (\sqrt{2x}+1\right )^{2}+\left (\sqrt{2x}-1\right )^{2}}$

$=\frac{4\sqrt{2x}}{2+4x}=\frac{2\sqrt{2x}}{1+2x}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: An engine of a train, moving with uniform acceleration, passes the signal-post with velocity u and the last compartment with velocity v. The velocity with which middle point of the train passes the signal post is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


 Let initial speed of train u. When midpoint of the train reach the signal post it's velocity becomes $v_{0}$.

$\therefore$ $v_{0}^{2}=u^{2}+2as$ .......(1)

When train passes the signal post completely it's velocity becomes v.

$\therefore$ $v^{2}=v_{0}^{2}+2as$ ......(2)

Subtracting (2) from (1) we get,

$v_{0}^{2}-v^{2}=u^{2}-v_{0}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow v_{0}^{2}+v_{0}^{2}=u^{2}+v^{2}$

$\Rightarrow v_{0}=\sqrt{\frac{u^{2}+v^{2}}{2}}$

text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.

Assertion A : When a rod lying freely is heated, no thermal stress is developed in it.

Reason R : On heating, the length of the rod increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and B are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Thermal stress develops only when thermal expansion is prevented; for a rod clamped at both ends it equals $Yα\Delta T$.

A rod lying freely is not restrained, so it expands without hindrance and no thermal stress develops: A is true.

On heating, the length of a rod increases by $\Delta L=Lα\Delta T$: R is true.

The length increases whether or not the rod is free, and in a clamped rod that same tendency is what produces stress; A follows from the absence of restraint, not from the increase in length, so R is not the correct explanation of A.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: If the time period of a two meter long simple pendulum is 2s, the acceleration due to gravity at the place where pendulum is executing S.H.M. is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The formula for the period of a simple pendulum is given by:

$T=2π\sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}$

where:

T is the period of the pendulum,
l is the length of the pendulum, and
g is the acceleration due to gravity.

We need to find g. Rearranging the formula for g, we get:

$g=\frac{4π^{2}l}{T^{2}}$

Given:

l = 2 m,
T = 2 s,

Substituting these values into the equation, we get:

$g=\frac{4π^{2}\times 2}{(2)^{2}}=2π^{2}ms^{-2}$

text:
In an octagon ABCDEFGH of equal side, what is the sum of 

$AB\leftarrow +AC\leftarrow +AD\leftarrow +AE\leftarrow +AF\leftarrow +AG\leftarrow +AH\leftarrow$,

if, $AO\leftarrow =2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\widehat{k}$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\because$ $OA\leftarrow +OB\leftarrow +OC\leftarrow +OD\leftarrow +OE\leftarrow +OF\leftarrow +OG\leftarrow +OH\leftarrow =\vec{0}$

By triangle law of vector addition, we can write

$AB\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OB\leftarrow ;AC\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OC\leftarrow$

$AD\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OD\leftarrow ;AE\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OE\leftarrow$

$AF\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OF\leftarrow ;AG\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OG\leftarrow$

$AH\leftarrow =AO\leftarrow +OH\leftarrow$

Now

$AB\leftarrow +AC\leftarrow +AD\leftarrow +AE\leftarrow +AF\leftarrow +AG\leftarrow +AH\leftarrow$

$=(7AO\leftarrow )+OB\leftarrow +OC\leftarrow +OD\leftarrow +OE\leftarrow +OF\leftarrow +OG\leftarrow +OH\leftarrow$

$=(7AO\leftarrow )+\vec{0}-OA\leftarrow$

$=(7AO\leftarrow )+AO\leftarrow$

$=8AO\leftarrow =8(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\widehat{k})$

$=16\hat{i}+24\hat{j}-32\widehat{k}$

text:
The current (i) at time t = 0 and t = $\infty$ respectively for the given circuit is :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
At $t=0$ the inductor carries no current, so its branch is open. Between the battery terminals there are then two paths in parallel: $5+1=6\Omega$ on the left and $5+4=9\Omega$ on the right.

$R_{0}=\dfrac{6\times 9}{6+9}=\dfrac{18}{5}\Omega \Rightarrow i(0)=\dfrac{E}{R_{0}}=\dfrac{5E}{18}$

At $t=\infty$ the inductor acts as a plain wire and joins the left and right junctions.


[IMG]

The two $5\Omega$ resistors are then in parallel between the upper battery terminal and this junction, and the $1\Omega$ and $4\Omega$ resistors are in parallel between the junction and the lower battery terminal.


[IMG]

$R_{\infty }=\dfrac{5\times 5}{5+5}+\dfrac{1\times 4}{1+4}=\dfrac{5}{2}+\dfrac{4}{5}=\dfrac{33}{10}\Omega \Rightarrow i(\infty )=\dfrac{10E}{33}$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: A small bob tied at one end of a thin string of length 1 m is describing a vertical circle so that the maximum and minimum tension in the string are in the ratio 5 : 1. The velocity of the bob at the highest position is $________ m/s. ($Take $g = 10 m/s^{2})$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


 Let the speed of bob at lowest position be $v_{1}$ and at the highest position be $v_{2}$.

Maximum tension is at lowest position and minimum tension is at the highest position. Now, using, conservation of mechanical energy,

$\frac{1}{2}mv_{1}^{2}=\frac{1}{2}mv_{2}^{2}+mg2l$

$\Rightarrow v_{1}^{2}=v_{2}^{2}+4gl$ ..........(1)

Now, $T_{\max }-mg=\frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{l}$

$\Rightarrow T_{\max }=mg+\frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{l}$

& $T_{\min }+mg=\frac{mv_{2}^{2}}{l}$

$\Rightarrow T_{\min }=\frac{mv_{2}^{2}}{l}-mg$

$\frac{T_{\max }}{T_{\min }}=\frac{5}{1}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{mg+\frac{mv2 1}{l}}{\frac{mv2 2}{l}-mg}=\frac{5}{1}$

$\Rightarrow mg+\frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{l}=\left [\frac{mv_{2}^{2}}{l}-mg\right ]5$

$\Rightarrow mg+\frac{m}{l}\left [v_{2}^{2}+4gl\right ]=\frac{5mv_{2}^{2}}{l}-5mg$

$\Rightarrow mg+\frac{mv_{2}^{2}}{l}+4mg=\frac{5mv_{2}^{2}}{l}-5mg$

$\Rightarrow 10mg=\frac{4mv_{2}^{2}}{l}$

$v_{2}^{2}=\frac{10\times 10\times 1}{4}$

$\Rightarrow v_{2}^{2}=25\Rightarrow v_{2}=5$ m/s

Thus, velocity of bob at highest position 5 m/s.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

text: A monoatomic gas of mass 4.0 u is kept in an insulated container. Container is moving with velocity 30 m/s. If container is suddenly stopped then change in temperature of the gas (R = gas constant) is $\frac{x}{3R}$. Value of x is $___________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
To find the change in temperature of a monoatomic gas when the container it is in is suddenly stopped, we can follow these steps:

Relationship Between Kinetic Energy and Internal Energy Change:  

The kinetic energy lost by the container when it stops is converted into the internal energy of the gas:

$\Delta KE=\Delta U$

Expression for Internal Energy Change:  

The change in internal energy can be expressed in terms of the change in temperature:

$\Delta U=nC_{v}\Delta T$

where $n$ is the number of moles, $C_{v}$ is the molar heat capacity at constant volume, and $\Delta T$ is the change in temperature.

Using the Kinetic Energy Formula for the Change:  

For a monoatomic gas, the molar heat capacity at constant volume $C_{v}$ is $\frac{3R}{2}$. Thus, we equate the kinetic energy to the change in internal energy:

$\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}=\frac{3}{2}nR\Delta T$

Solving for $\Delta T$:  

Rearrange the equation to solve for the change in temperature:

$\Delta T=\frac{mv^{2}}{3nR}$

Substituting Given Values:  

Here, mass $m=4$ u, velocity $v=30$ m/s, and the number of moles $n=1$. Substitute these into the equation:

$\Delta T=\frac{4\times (30)^{2}}{3\times 1\times R}$

Simplifying:

$\Delta T=\frac{1200}{R}$

Relating to Given Expression:  

According to the problem, $\Delta T=\frac{x}{3R}$. Therefore, equating:

$\frac{x}{3R}=\frac{1200}{R}$

Solve for $x$:  

Simplifying gives:

$x=3600$

Thus, the value of $x$ is 3600.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift

solution.body:

text: In a certain thermodynamical process, the pressure of a gas depends on its volume as $kV^{3}$. The work done when the temperature changes from 100${}^{\circ }$C to 300${}^{\circ }$C will be $___________ nR$, where n denotes number of moles of a gas.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In this thermodynamical process, the pressure $P$ of a gas is related to its volume $V$ by the equation $P=kV^{3}$. Thus, we have:

$PV^{-3}=k$

This implies that the value of $x$ is $-3$ in the relationship. To find the work done ($W$) when the temperature changes from 100°C to 300°C, we can use the formula:

$W=\frac{nR(T_{1}-T_{2})}{x-1}$

Substitute the given temperatures and the value of $x$:

$W=\frac{nR(100-300)}{-3-1}$

Calculate the expression:

$W=\frac{nR(-200)}{-4}$

Which simplifies to:

$W=50nR$

text: 512 identical drops of mercury are charged to a potential of 2V each. The drops are joined to form a single drop. The potential of this drop is $________ V$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let charge on each drop = q

radius = r

$v=\frac{kq}{r}$

$\Rightarrow$ $2=\frac{kq}{r}$

radius of bigger

$\frac{4}{3}πR^{3}=512\times \frac{4}{3}πr^{3}$

$R=8r$

$\therefore$ $v=\frac{k(512)q}{R}=\frac{512}{8}\frac{kq}{r}=\frac{512}{8}\times 2$

$=128V$

text: A transmitting station releases waves of wavelength 960 m. A capacitor of 2.56 $μ$F is used in the resonant circuit. The self inductance of coil necessary for resonance is $__________$ $\times$ $10^{-8} H$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th February Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$λ$ = 960 m

C = 2.56 $μ$F = 2.56 $\times$ $10^{-6}^{} F$

c = 3 $\times$ $10^{8} m/s$

L = ?

Now at resonance, $ω_{0}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

[Resonant frequency]

$2πf_{0}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

On substituting $f_{0}=\frac{c}{λ}$, we have $2π\frac{c}{λ}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

Squaring both sides : $4π^{2}\frac{c^{2}}{λ^{2}}=\frac{1}{LC}$

$=\frac{4\times 10\times (3\times 10^{8})^{2}}{(960)^{2}}=\frac{1}{L\times 2.56\times 10^{-6}}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{L}=\frac{4\times 10\times 9\times 10^{16}\times 2.56\times 10^{-6}}{960\times 960}$

$\Rightarrow L=10\times 10^{-8}$ H
